Disputed by: 2021A&A...645A.127G: Sect. 5.1-5.2: GRAVITY CLEAN imaging in 2019 finds a slowly moving mK = 18.9 star within 30 mas of Sgr A* whose position and proper motion best match S62 (Gillessen et al. 2017 numbering), at |z| > 150 mas from the lack of acceleration. Peißker's 9.9 yr orbit predicts (RA, Dec) = (-89..-85, +98..+95) mas with ~(+7,-5) mas/yr; GRAVITY pointed there on 13-14 Aug and 13 Sep 2019 and found a single mK ~ 16.6 source moving ~(+21,-46) mas/yr that 'match[es] perfectly the orbital trace of the star S29'. 'We cannot report the detection of any object that would correspond to the 9.9-year orbit'; they speculate S29 was misidentified as S62 in NACO images.; 2022A&A...657A..82G: Sect. 4.2: GRAVITY's S62 re-detected in all 2021 nights, linear motion vRA = 2.97 +/- 0.05, vDec = -3.58 +/- 0.09 mas/yr; 'does not fit a star with a 9.9 year orbital period as reported in Peißker et al. Appendix D.2-D.3: h_z of S29 excludes identity with 'S62Peissker'; no counterpart found in the 2019 S29 pointings or the 2021 north-west mosaic pointing.; 2022A&A...657L..12G: Fig. 1 caption: the 2021 central GRAVITY field is dominated by S29, S55, S62 and S300 (S62 K = 18.9) - i.e. GRAVITY's S62, not Peißker's. Not an independent argument; follows A127/A82.; 2026Natur.657..359A: Methods (S301 discovery, GRAVITY+): 'we can exclude that the objects in ref. 49 [2020ApJ...899...50P] named S4711 and S62 (different from the star our team calls S62; see ref. 51 [2021A&A...645A.127G]) ... are actually S301'; Peißker's S62 orbit 'revolves anticlockwise, unlike S301'.
